newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs close lower, profit-taking gnaws gains.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs close lower, profit-taking gnaws gains.

text.p: Shares closed Friday's trading slightly lower after profit-taking eroded the gains of the previous two days, brokers said.

They added that they expected the index to decline further on Saturday on rumours that the government had no intention to boost the market in the short-term. The composite stock index fell 3.42 points to a provisional close of 733.50 by midday.

"There was talk that the government met with the ruling New Korea party this afternoon, and they decided long-term measures to improve the stock market was preferable to a quick fix," said a local fund manager.
The finance ministry has said it doesn't comment on market rumours. Decliners nosed ahead of advancers 466 to 400, while volume was a thin 22.7 million.
"I see a further consolidation for the market for the time being. The downside risk is limited but the upside is also slim," said a Dongsuh Securities broker.
"November was the worst month for the market, but I think December will be a little better," he added.
Poor economic indicators pressured the market. The central bank said October's current account deficit soared to $2.41 billion from a $340.5 million shortfall a year ago.

The bank also revised upward its projection for the year's current account deficit to about $21.5 billion from an earlier forecast of about $20 billion. Last year, the deficit came in at $8.95 billion.
Brokers said foreigners actively sold banking and securities shares. Cho Hung Bank topped the actives list, losing 140 won to 6,520.

"This is a bad sign, considering how oversold bank shares are," said the Dongsuh broker. "It means that foreigners are taking money out of Seoul because they think it will take time for the next rally."
